# Career Preparation and Next Steps

## Overview
The final day turns your new skills into a job search strategy and a plan for continued growth. First, understand the landscape: 'data science' spans several roles, data analyst (focused on SQL, dashboards, and business insight), data scientist (statistics, ML, and experimentation), ML engineer (productionizing models), and data engineer (building data pipelines), and knowing which fits your interests helps you target the right jobs and tailor your resume. Your resume and LinkedIn should emphasize projects and measurable results, not just a list of tools, and link to your portfolio and GitHub. Interview preparation is crucial because DS interviews are broad: expect SQL query challenges, statistics and probability questions, ML concept questions (like explaining the bias-variance tradeoff or how a Random Forest works), a take-home or case study where you analyze a problem, and behavioral questions about how you work. Practicing these deliberately, using platforms for SQL and ML questions and mock interviews, makes a big difference. Finally, data science is a field of continuous learning: plan your next steps, deepen a specialization, take on harder projects, contribute to open source, and keep learning, so this 45-day roadmap becomes the launchpad for a long, evolving career.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Data science roles and specializations; Resume and LinkedIn optimization; Technical and case interview preparation; Practicing SQL, ML, and behavioral questions; A continued learning roadmap. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Update your resume and LinkedIn to highlight your projects and results, then complete a mock interview covering one SQL question, one ML concept question, and one behavioral question.
Mini Project: Create a personalized job-search kit: a targeted resume, an optimized LinkedIn summary, a list of 10 target roles/companies, and a 3-month continued-learning plan for your chosen specialization.
Assignment: Write out and answer five common data science interview questions (mixing SQL, statistics, ML, and behavioral) as if in a real interview.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.

## Assessment
After finishing the work, open the AI Assessment popup to submit your practical results. DeepSeek will evaluate your submission, calculate a dynamic score based on correctness and depth, and add the points to your CalibiAI profile.
